history.summary: Navagraha shrine in Ujjain dedicated to the nine celestial deities (grahas). Wikipedia notes a long-established Navagraha temple inside the Bada Ganpati Temple complex just behind the Mahakaleshwar Temple towards Harsiddhi, where devotees worship all nine planets, offer mustard oil and flowers to Shani, and do parikrama of the Navagraha stones. A separate listing describes a 'Shree Nav Grah Shani Temple' on the banks of the Triveni Sangam claiming 2,000-year antiquity by King Vikramaditya — which of these the CSV row refers to is UNVERIFIED; coordinates here are approximate and may correspond to the Triveni Sangam shrine. Timings conflict across sources (verify before visiting).

name: Navagraha Temple
town_description: Ujjain is an ancient city on the eastern bank of the Shipra (Kshipra) River in the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh, one of the seven Sapta Puri sacred cities of Hinduism. It is home to the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga, hosts the Simhastha Kumbh Mela every 12 years, and was the prime meridian for Hindu geographers since the 4th century BCE. Formerly Ujjayini, capital of the Avanti Kingdom, it remains a major Shaiva and Shakti pilgrimage centre.
